title: DynamAuction: A Reinforcement Learning Environment for Repeated Auctions with Dynamic Value
claim: A repeated interaction loop between agent and environment, with initialization and four cyclic stages, defines the whole sequential decision process.
layout: Initialization banner above a 2x2 cycle of boxes, clockwise arrows
description: A wide gray Initialization banner sits at the top. It lists the sampled user u, the horizon T, the auction times {θ_j} and the initial display x_1, each with its distribution. Below it, four pastel boxes form a 2x2 clockwise cycle joined by dark blue arrows. Box 1 (lavender, Observation) gives the buyer's observed state Z_j as a tuple. Box 2 (green, Buyer) has the policy choose the bid b_j = π(Z_j). Box 3 (peach, Auction) samples the price to beat B_j and reveals the win indicator W_j and price p_j. Box 4 (mauve, Environment update) updates the carry-over state S_u after a win, generates rewards and advances to the next auction time. The arrow from box 4 back to box 1 closes the loop. The eye goes first to the numbered, bolded box titles. Math notation fills every box.
caption: Overview of DynamAuction, illustrating the interaction between the bidding agent and the environment, the dependence of future values on past wins, and the timing of rewards.
abstract: A buyer who repeatedly participates in auctions for related items often faces a dynamic value problem: what they win today changes what tomorrow's items are worth. Despite the empirical importance of such effects, especially in display advertising, the algorithmic literature on repeated auctions has largely focused on the learning problem, by treating each opportunity as a contextual bandit, while sidestepping the planning problem induced by the dependence of current value on past wins. We introduce DynamAuction, a synthetic environment for single-buyer sequential bidding. The reward from each win depends on the buyer's history of previous wins, summarized through a carry-over state. The environment supports first- and second-price auctions, non-homogeneous Poisson arrivals, delayed feedback, saturation, and recency effects. We also introduce a new class of Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithms. On our benchmark scenario, these MPC policies outperform off-the-shelf deep RL baselines (PPO, SAC, TD3) as well as a tuned shading baseline. We release DynamAuction to support RL research on repeated auctions.
